text:
alex: Heads-up — Sales looped us in with LumenFin. They want firm SLAs for an upcoming pilot. Product asked for p95 120ms, Sales pushed p99 250ms. We need a quick tradeoff sketch.
meera: do we have profiling for their workload shape? short chats, avg seq len 60, ~10% long tails (>=512). QPS expected 1200 rps steady, spikes to 3k.
sam: I ran a microbatch sweep yesterday. Summary:
```
kernel A (opt matmul): microbatch=8 -> p95=95ms p99=220ms tput=~1100
kernel A: microbatch=4 -> p95=70ms p99=160ms tput=700
kernel B (quantized path): microbatch=8 -> p95=110ms p99=270ms tput=1200
KV cache warm: p95 drop ~20-30ms across configs; cold misses add ~80-120ms
```
meera: interesting — kernel A microbatch=4 hits Product p95 120ms easily, but throughput drops. Sales will hate the lower tput.
jordan: For LumenFin they care about 99th more than throughput — fraud checks need bounded tails. Any way to improve p99 without killing tput?
sam: KV cache is biggest lever. If we ensure warm rate >85% p99 improves ~40-60ms. Also a tiny kernel tweak: prefer matmul-fused path for seq<256, fall back for longer sequences. That buys ~30ms more at p99.
ben: So combined approach: microbatch=6, kernel A for short, kernel B fallback, aggressive KV prewarm for VIP customers. What are numbers?
sam: Rough estimate: microbatch=6 -> p95 ~85ms p99 ~180-200ms at steady tput~950. With KV warm >90% -> p99 -> ~140-160ms.
alex: Sales-bot, can you confirm LumenFin will accept reserved warm-up period and modest throughput carveout?
sales-bot: @sales rep pinged: LumenFin says they can tolerate a 30-minute warmup window per deploy if it guarantees p99 <= 180ms for peak windows. They want monthly SLA with credit.
meera: That sounds workable. Ops questions: how do we enforce warm-up? Prepopulate KV with typical prefixes from their corpus + synthetic priming?
sam: We can seed per-customer KV by replaying last 24h heavy queries or run a warmup harness hitting hot prefixes. Need an API hook from Sales to share top prompt clusters (anonymized).
jordan: Also need a rollout plan: canary at 10% then 50% with active monitoring on p99 and kv-warm-rate. If p99 regresses >10% rollback.
alex: TL;DR proposal to Product/Sales:
- Offer two SLA tiers: "Balanced" (p95 <=120ms, p99 <=220ms, baseline tput ~1100) and "TailGuard" (p95 <=120ms, p99 <=180ms with 30min warmup & reserved capacity, tput ~950).
- Tech mitigations: microbatch sizing 4-6, kernel routing by seq len, KV prewarm/seeding, canary rollout + auto rollback.
meera: I'll draft the SLA language and required warmup playbook. Sam/Jordan please attach perf graphs and the warmup script.
sam: attaching quick perf snippet (link) and will push warmup harness to repo: infra/warmers/lumenfin-warmup.sh
ben: one caveat — burst spikes to 3k still risk queueing; suggest burst buffers or short-lived instances to absorb, with cost tradeoff explained to Sales.
meera: good call. Sales, include burst buffer pricing in the proposal.
sales-bot: noted. LumenFin rep okayed reviewing a pricing table with burst buffer option.
alex: thanks team — product/sales meeting at 10am PT. Bring numbers.
meera: will do. Short action list: Sam -> perf charts + warmup script; Jordan -> canary + rollback thresholds; Ben -> capacity plan cost delta; meera -> SLA draft.
sam: on it. will post updated numbers before 09:30.
ben: also logging one perf regression we saw last week: kernel B path shows 15% p99 increase after latest cudnn upgrade; created issue #3217. Keep in mind when we recommend fallback rules.
jordan: thanks — will add guardrail to routing policy to avoid path on that cudnn version.
alex: perfect.
